finding.description: The branch already had call-scoped effect re-entry binding and a PreToolUse/PostToolUse adapter keyed by tool_use_id, but no dedicated regression exercised two semantically identical calls in one session whose PostToolUse events close in reverse order. That is the minimal source falsifier for a hidden mutable session-scoped current-effect router.
finding.counterhypothesis: The existing call-scoped adapter is sufficient and reverse-order same-session completion remains correctly bound without a dedicated regression.
finding.discriminator: Create two same-session same-tool same-input PreToolUse requests with distinct tool_use_id values, close B before A, and require a transplanted B post-event against A to fail closed on INVOCATION_ID_MISMATCH.

cases: same-session identical calls close in reverse order without cross-talk
PostToolUseFailure preserves exact call-scoped invocation identity
missing PreToolUse tool_use_id fails closed without session fallback

transport_boundary.effect: Do not bypass with a duplicate dispatch, generation advance, provider call, or paid fallback.

next_exact_action: Preserve issues 2122 and 2121 as the singleton runtime gates. Restore the already-established self-hosted Linux/X64 runner/host bridge when an authorized host-control surface is actually available, then consume the existing queued results rather than redispatching. In the non-conflicting source lane, bind the new hook invocation reverse-order regression into the next explicitly admitted deterministic Frankenstein-2.0 regression capsule and execute it only on an admitted zero-cost surface; no runtime credit until that execution exists.
